scope: Proposition 5.9 (Critical sphere cuts) of the manuscript “The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4” (preprints/The-critical-Liouville-quantum-sphere-and-geometric-limits-of-FK-maps-at-q-equals-4-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b9236021eab20eb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 66. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the unit-area critical sphere of Section 2 with an independent nested CLE4, the counting intensity of a loop, a fair choice of side, its intrinsic perimeter s, and that side’s area v has density 1 2π2 s−5 ds(v)ds(1 − v) ds dv, s > 0, 0 < v < 1. The corresponding actual cut surfaces are the critical disk pair with these areas and perimeter, with independent uniform relative boundary phase and independent nested CLEs in the two interiors. Matching is by the intrinsic boundary-length labels. The identity also holds, after integrating scale, as a measure-class identity for arbitrary total area. No uniqueness theorem for critical conformal welding is required.
